fr.recommendations:
• Install a clearly visible address marker at the driveway entrance that can be read from both directions of travel on the street.
• Mark the single driveway entrance with reflective posts or markers to help responders locate it quickly at night or in low visibility conditions.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges to maintain a clear travel path wide enough for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back trees or shrubs overhanging the driveway to provide vertical clearance for fire and rescue apparatus.
• Thin dense vegetation between the street and the main residence so responders can see the structure from the road.
• Remove or trim vegetation growing directly against the main residence and detached structure to keep those walls clear for responders working close to the buildings.
• Keep the walkway between the main residence and detached structure clear of vegetation and obstructions so responders can move between the two buildings on foot.
• Identify and mark any available secondary foot access point to the rear of the property, even if vehicle access is not possible.
• Keep a gate or opening at the rear of the property unlocked or fitted with a Knox-Box style lock to allow responders to reach the rear without returning to the front.
• Maintain the parking area clear of stored vehicles or equipment that would block responders from positioning apparatus close to the main residence.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back tree branches that overhang or touch the house on all sides.
• Thin the cluster of trees closest to the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants growing directly against the house walls.
• Separate the vegetation around the structure by cutting back plants to create open ground between them and the house.
• Thin the second tree cluster to reduce the concentration of trees in that area.
• Remove dead branches from scattered trees near the structure.
• Cut back scattered shrubs near the house to reduce the amount of burnable material close to the building.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along both sides.
• Maintain the open clearing by keeping it free of shrubs and tree seedlings that may be establishing there.
• Keep the ground beneath large trees near the house clear of dead leaves, fallen branches, and dry plant material.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate from the road, especially under low-visibility conditions.
